long_biography.plain_text:
Born in Brooklyn, David Geffen entered entertainment through the William Morris Agency mailroom. He advanced to agent and manager, representing a generation of singer-songwriters before launching Asylum Records around artists he believed labels had overlooked. Geffen Records and DGC followed, widening his influence across popular music. He also formed Geffen Pictures and joined Steven Spielberg and Jeffrey Katzenberg to establish DreamWorks.

The later chapter of Geffen's career has been shaped by arts and education philanthropy. Through his foundation, he supported tuition-free study at Yale's drama school, making professional theatrical training accessible without the burden of tuition. That commitment extends the talent-building instinct behind his early management and label work into a lasting educational institution for actors, directors, designers and other theatre makers.
